newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- March 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
* South Africa's police force, which struck terror in people during apartheid, has shown itself to be corrupt, barely literate and inept.
* Canada's arrest of a Saudi Arabian citizen could be a major breakthrough in a U.S. investigation into a bombing at a military base in Saudi Arabia which killed 19 Americans.
* During his visit to China, Vice President Al Gore will preside over the signing of two business deals, worth nearly $2 billion, including China's purchase of five Boeing jetliners for $685 million.

* Administration officials said the White House tried to get sensitive counterintelligence information about Beijing's plans to sway American politics but was denied by Director Louis Freeh of the Federal Bureau of Investigations.

* Outlying regions in Russia, frustrated by Moscow's inability to pay wages, build houses and maintain hospitals and roads, are turning their back on the new Russian constitution and withholding taxes.
* A New York City subway clerk, age 60 and less than two years away from retirement, was killed at a station he chose because he thought it would be safer.
* Spanglish - a linguistic blend of English and Spanish - is becoming the language of choice for many Hispanic Americans.
* The U.S. Supreme Court will decide under what circumstances one state's courts can refuse to abide by the rulings of another state's courts.
